main_issue: Whether to restrict strong-smelling cooking (D's fish curry) in the shared kitchen, and whether a time-based rule (no cooking before 7 p.m. weekdays) is enough.

A-B.evidence: B backed A's ban at turn 2, but by turns 22-25 B rejects A's narrow before-7pm proposal as 'not a separate issue'; A insists it's separate (turn 24).

A-C.evidence: C agreed at turn 3, but at turns 9, 15 and 23 says timing doesn't matter, which conflicts with A's time-limited proposal; A never concedes.

A-D.evidence: A narrowed from a blanket ban to weekdays before 7pm (turns 11, 17), which is a partial concession; D still objects ('So what am I supposed to do? Not cook?', turn 16).

B-C.evidence: B and C echo each other throughout (turns 8-9, 14-15, 22-23); C says 'She's right' at 23.

B-D.evidence: D resists restrictions and says all must cook (turn 10). B still wants a rule covering all times. D does cite B's point (turn 12) but only as a tactic, not as agreement.

C-D.evidence: C's laundry complaint continues (turns 9, 15, 23), while D resists limits on cooking (turns 10, 16).
